name: Oath of Greed
body:
Antipaladins who embrace a lavish lifestyle; these individuals want more, more, MORE! And their bottomless hunger for fame and fortune leads them down a dark and endless spiral.

The oath of greed is an archetype of the antipaladin class.

Code of Conduct

Antipaladins who follow the ways of greed always seek some way to gain more of what they desire. This doesn’t always have to be material, but their desire must be unwavering.

They can never give to charity or freely offer up their own goods without good reason. Giving an ally a magic item which benefits them and makes them stronger is acceptable, as making one’s ally stronger indirectly benefits the oathbound antipaladin. However, giving away gold or other valuables purely to help another creature would violate this code.

An antipaladin who violates this code loses all class features from this archetype until they atone (see the atonement spell).

Covetous Aura (Su)

At 3rd level, the oath of greed antipaladin exudes a field of corrupt temptation. Creatures within 10 feet are filled with urges of kleptomania, compelling them to steal. Activating this aura is a swift action, and it can be used once per day, lasting a number of rounds equal to 3 + the antipaladin’s Charisma modifier.

Creatures within the aura must succeed at a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the antipaladin’s level + the antipaladin’s Charisma modifier) or be afflicted as if covetous urge had been cast upon them, using the antipaladin’s level as the caster level. Unlike the spell, this effect is not language-dependent and doesn’t require a material component.

This ability replaces aura of cowardice.

Gilded Smite (Su)

At 5th level, whenever an oath of greed antipaladin declares a smite good, their strike manifests their hunger for wealth. On the first successful attack each round against a smite target, the foe must succeed at a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the antipaladin’s level + the antipaladin’s Charisma modifier) or drop one object they are currently carrying (starting with the most valuable item if multiple are held). If no such object is available, the target instead takes a -2 penalty on saving throws against compulsion effects and a -4 to CMD against steal and disarm combat maneuvers for a number of rounds equal to half the antipaladin’s level (minimum of 1 round).

This ability modifies smite good.

Dragon’s Hoard (Su)

At 17th level, the oath of greed antipaladin’s lust for wealth begins to compete with the likes of dragons. For every 10,000 gp worth of gear in their possession, they gain a +1 profane bonus to AC and saving throws (maximum of +5). This adds together the value of armor, weapons, and worn gear however it does not factor in consumables or material components such as potions or diamond dust.

In addition, the antipaladin has a hoard of wealth stored somewhere (such as a bank or their personal home) where they have their money held. For every 50,000 gp worth of coins, gems, art objects, and trade goods secured in a single location they declare as their hoard they gain a +1 profane bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, caster level checks, and saving throw DCs. This bonus cannot exceed +5, and is lost if the hoard is dispersed, stolen, or destroyed. The antipaladin must personally claim the site as their hoard, and may only benefit from one hoard as a time.

This ability replaces aura of depravity.
